Tagcast 0.40.0 adds streaming quality controls, native album ratings and playlists,
Play next and repeat, optional listening history, cover enlargement and optional
queue synchronisation. All features are included in the standalone downloads for
macOS, Windows and Linux.

## Playback and streaming quality

- **Settings → Playback → Streaming quality** chooses MP3 96/128/192/256/320 kbps
  or Original. Free accounts use 128 kbps; every other choice requires Premium.
  The preference applies to the next track. The player distinguishes the uploaded
  **File** format from the requested **Stream** quality. If Original cannot play
  in your browser, Tagcast tries MP3 128 kbps once and labels the fallback.
- The **+ ▾** menu offers **Add to queue**, **Play next** and, for a single track,
  **Add to playlist…**. Album actions include every disc in order. Play next keeps
  additions in click order and returns to the original queue afterwards.
- **Repeat** cycles Off → Queue → Track, preserving album order. **Save as
  playlist…** keeps the queue as a native playlist after review.
- Double-click a cover in the album grid/list, album details or the player to
  open a lightbox. Larger artwork loads on demand; Escape, × or the backdrop
  closes it without changing playback or browser history.

## Album ratings and playlists

- Albums have native **0–5 star ratings** and a favourite heart. **Album
  favourites** lists five-star albums; a merged set appears when every disc is
  rated five. Requested stars/hearts appear immediately with saving/checking
  feedback. Confirmation updates the page without a manual refresh.
- **Playlists** supports creating private playlists, playing them in order,
  renaming, reviewing track removals, adding an album and saving/appending the
  queue. A track's **+ ▾ → Add to playlist…** adds only that track; Now playing
  also offers **Add this track to playlist…**.
- **Delete playlist…** reviews the name and track count before deleting the
  playlist definition. Its music stays in your library and playback continues.
  System playlists and folders are protected.
- Collection writes check the current values and read back the result. Changed
  previews are rejected; uncertain creation, append or deletion requests are
  never automatically retried. Ratings and playlists stay separate from metadata
  Change history and its Undo.

## Settings and optional iBroadcast listening history

- **Sources & keys** is now **Settings**. The library information banner has a
  dismiss button; restore it through **Settings → Interface**. The preference
  stays in this browser.
- **Record played tracks in iBroadcast** is **off by default**. When enabled,
  Tagcast sends a track ID and timestamp after more than ten seconds of actual
  listening. Pauses, buffering and seeks do not count; earlier plays and skips
  are not sent. Uncertain requests are not retried automatically. Tagcast itself
  does not send Last.fm scrobbles.
- Enabling reporting shows **Recently played**, using iBroadcast's native recent
  tracks playlist, including plays from other devices. Search, paging and manual
  refresh are available. Each track appears once, most recent first; iBroadcast
  supplies no play timestamps in this playlist.
- Metadata **History** is now **Change history**, with **Export changes**, to
  distinguish saved edits from listening history.

## Optional queue synchronisation and remote control

- **Settings → Devices & queue synchronisation** enables a separate extension,
  **off by default** and independent of play reporting. Reconnect iBroadcast to
  approve the additional queue read/write permissions, then explicitly connect
  through **Devices**.
- Restore a saved queue with an explicit choice to play, or control an available
  device's queue, playback, position, volume and repeat. A controller pauses local
  audio, reports no plays and never advances the remote track on its own.
- One browser tab owns the connection. WebSocket and OAuth tokens stay on the
  local server; reconnects obtain fresh one-use tokens. Library notifications
  offer a manual reload. Device compatibility depends on its active iBroadcast
  session and approved queue permissions.

## Appearance and duplicate detection

- The original **Powered by iBroadcast** branding is compact at the bottom of
  the sidebar; the version appears beside Tagcast at the top. Navigation icons
  use a consistent style.
- Duplicate candidates now ignore straight/curly quotation-mark differences as
  well as case and spacing. The same positive track number and disc are still
  required; version text and other punctuation remain significant. Candidates
  are metadata matches, not an audio or quality comparison. Trash moves still
  require review and never delete permanently.
- The README includes the latest feature instructions, screenshots and Homebrew
  installation steps. Source start scripts upgrade an older environment when
  the new WebSocket dependency is missing.

## Standalone downloads and updating

- **macOS Apple Silicon:** `tagcast-0.40.0-macos-arm64.zip`.
- **macOS Intel:** `tagcast-0.40.0-macos-x64.zip`.
- **Windows x64:** `tagcast-0.40.0-windows-x64.zip`.
- **Linux x64:** `tagcast-0.40.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

Each archive bundles Python, dependencies, a desktop launcher, a separate CLI
and license notices, with a companion SHA-256 checksum. Extract the whole package;
move `Tagcast.app` to Applications on macOS, open `Tagcast.exe` on Windows, or run
`./Tagcast` inside the extracted Linux folder. macOS and Windows downloads remain
unsigned by Developer ID/Authenticode; the README explains the normal first-launch
security steps.

**Stop the old Tagcast before starting 0.40.0**, and let any cleanup finish or stop
it first. Otherwise the new launcher opens the already-running server. Your
settings, tokens and cache stay in `~/.tagcast/`, or your configured `TAGCAST_HOME`.
Source installations remain supported with Python 3.11+ or uv.

For Homebrew, stop Tagcast, then run `brew update` and
`brew upgrade --cask cyberdeliaAI/apps/tagcast` once the tap has the new checksums.

See the [README](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v0.40.0/README.md)
and [standalone guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v0.40.0/docs/native-builds.md)
for installation and feature details. Your local music files are never changed.
